report: PyShield Round 3 fifth-material review (post-fix verification, audit template)
verdict_reason: PSH-R5-001 is closed by three independent layers (release tree without caches, import-time cache isolation, manifest rejection of unsigned bytecode) and reproduces as rc=1 with no marker. PSH-R5-002 now fails closed without key needles and rejects __pycache__ in trees and zips; a random key in a bare zip without --secret remains undecidable by design. No new exploitable issue was found; one informational build-path leak was fixed in the same commit. CI for d98b48e has not run yet and both executables are local builds.

ci_runs.detail: local only; push required before citing CI

findings.title: Challenge zip ships __pycache__ outside the signed manifest; a tampered pyc executes while the manifest passes
findings.preconditions: local write access to the deployment directory; no admin/debugger/memory dump required
findings.summary: The release no longer contains bytecode caches, the runtime redirects sys.pycache_prefix and disables cache writes before protected packages are imported, and _scan_integrity rejects any .pyc outside _shield_runtime. A planted demo/__pycache__ pyc now fails with 'unsigned bytecode cache' and never executes.
findings.root_cause: CPython validates timestamp-based pyc headers only against source mtime/size; the manifest covered .py files but not caches, and the packaging step shipped __pycache__.
repro_steps: Copy the challenge tree to a writable directory.
Write demo/__pycache__/__init__.cpython-312.pyc with a matching header and marker payload.
findings.impact: Before the fix a writable deployment allowed arbitrary code execution that bypassed the integrity promise. After the fix the forged cache is neither executed nor accepted.
evidence: logs/pycache-tamper-r5.log: rc=1, marker absent, 'unsigned bytecode cache'
logs/prefix-hijack-r5.log: PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX poison ignored, check rc=0
findings.remediation: manifest.collect_files(forbid_bytecode=True); builder.clean_pycache + assert_no_bytecode_caches; runtime _isolate_bytecode + _scan_bytecode_caches; check_release.py rejects caches.
findings.post_fix_verification: Reproduced with pycache_tamper_r5.py and prefix_hijack_r5.py; both behave as expected on the shipped zip.
findings.residual_risk: Replacing _shield_runtime or poisoning an attacker-chosen pycache prefix is out of scope; integrity=off builds keep import isolation only.

findings.title: check_release.py key coverage and pycache rejection were incomplete and overstated
findings.preconditions: release process relies on the checker; local user
findings.summary: The checker now takes --secret, discovers real secrets in TEMP, fails closed when no needles are available, and rejects __pycache__ / unlisted .pyc in trees and archives. A random key inside an archive with no secret source remains undecidable and is reported as such.
findings.root_cause: --temp passed empty needle tuples; archives without a sibling secret had no key source; neither path rejected bytecode caches.
repro_steps: Write a real master key into a pyshield*-named TEMP directory.
Run check_release.py --temp without --secret: must fail as 'cannot verify'.
Repeat with --secret: must report 'build key material'.
Add a __pycache__ entry to a copy of the challenge zip: must fail.
findings.impact: Before the fix the checker returned 0 without scanning keys and accepted caches, and the fix response treated '--temp 0' as proof of key hygiene.
evidence: logs/check-release-artifacts.log: both shipped zips pass with --skip-key-scan and a scoped OK message
findings.remediation: --secret/--skip-key-scan, TEMP secret discovery, fail-closed default, bytecode rejection, scoped success message.
findings.post_fix_verification: All five scenarios in check_release_gap_r5.py behave as expected.
findings.residual_risk: A random 32-byte key has no detectable shape; a bare archive without --secret can only fail closed, not prove absence of leakage.

findings.title: Runtime pyc co_filename leaked the build machine's temporary output path
findings.preconditions: read access to the deployed runtime pyc or a runtime traceback
findings.summary: Tracebacks from the runtime used to print the builder's temporary output directory; py_compile now receives a relative dfile.
findings.root_cause: compile_runtime passed dfile=str(source) while the source lived in the temporary build directory.
repro_steps: Trigger any runtime traceback and read the path.
findings.impact: Build-path disclosure only; no key or source disclosure.
findings.post_fix_verification: co_filename is relative on the shipped zip.
findings.residual_risk: PyInstaller built-in binaries may still carry symbols/paths (see R-15).
